name: Average guesstimate: city water use with a workable formula but thin scoping, leakage only when prompted, shallow check

messages.text: Estimate the total daily water consumption for a city of 5 million people.
Should I give the answer in liters per day?

Okay so I will start with households. Per person, you drink a couple of liters, a shower is maybe 50 liters, toilet flushes add up to maybe 30 or 40, cooking and washing dishes and clothes, so I will say around 150 liters per person per day. 5 million times 150 is 750 million liters a day.
No, there are also offices, schools, hospitals, restaurants. I will add about 20 percent for commercial, so 750 million plus 150 million is about 900 million liters a day.
What about industry, or water that is lost before it reaches anyone?

Right, I forgot about leaks. Pipes in a lot of cities lose a lot, I have heard numbers like 30 percent, so I will add 30 percent on top. 900 million times 1.3 is around 1.1 or 1.2 billion. Industry I guess is kind of included in the commercial part, so I will leave it.
Is 30 percent of the total or of the delivered water?
I just added it on top of what people use, so of the delivered amount. It is probably close either way.
Okay. Give me your final answer.
I would say about 1.1 billion liters a day, give or take. It seems reasonable for a city that size. It could be higher if the city is hot or has a lot of industry.
